feat: auto-quote paths with spaces for shell compatibility

When copying filesystem paths that contain spaces, Trimmy now
automatically wraps them in double quotes so they work correctly
with shell commands like `cd`.

Supported path formats:
- Absolute paths: /Users/name/My Documents
- Home-relative: ~/Library/Application Support
- Relative: ./My Project/src or folder/sub folder/file

The feature:
- Skips paths without spaces (no transformation needed)
- Skips already-quoted paths
- Skips URLs (containing ://)
- Skips command-like text (containing flags like -la)
- Escapes existing double quotes within paths

This solves the common pain point of copying paths from tools like
ripgrep and having them fail when pasted into terminal commands.
